title: Rising Prices Have People in Japan Dining Out Less
paragraphs: Prices for food and many other things have been going up in Japan. Because of this, many people are eating at restaurants less often, according to several surveys.

In one survey from May 2026, the research company System Research asked people in their 20s to 50s about eating out. It found that 62.0% of people had stopped themselves from eating out because of rising prices. Interestingly, about half of these people said that they had made their meals at home a little more luxurious instead.
Another online survey of 1,024 people, also from May, found that 45.4% of people said they were eating out less often than before.

When people do eat out, price is becoming a more important part of their decision about where to go. A survey by the company MS&Consulting asked 1,071 people aged 20 to 59 how they choose restaurants. For lunch, 57.2% said price was one of their main reasons for choosing a restaurant. In 2025, the number was 52.1%. For dinner with alcohol, 42.6% said price was important.
However, not all surveys found the same thing. A large survey by Cross Marketing found that the number of times people eat out was about the same as in 2024.
In addition, Japan's central bank, the Bank of Japan, also found in its own survey that people had spent less on eating out, clothing and travel than a year earlier.
